title: img2threejs 1.5.1: Turning a GLB into editable Three.js code
author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
selftext:
Trying a new workflow with **img2threejs**:

**Image → GLB → editable Three.js code**

The GLB is used only as a 3D reference. img2threejs reconstructs it into structured code you can edit, animate, and interact with.

comments.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
comments.body:
If you just need to render a GLB, load it directly. But if you want the model as code, this is where it gets interesting.

Showcase: [https://img2threejs.io/#/demo/warrior](https://img2threejs.io/#/demo/warrior)

Opensource: [https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs](https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs)

replies.author: reca11ed
replies.body: Most of the work is done by tripo3d? You went img -> glb using their service?

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
Not exactly. Tripo is used as part of the pipeline, but the final result is generated as pure Three.js code, not simply img → GLB.

The 1.5.1 flow is specifically about reconstructing the model directly into Three.js.

replies.author: reca11ed
replies.body: Does it work with non tripo3d glbs? I did a quick test and it did not because there weren’t named parts.

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body: Of course, tripo just an option, can I have your image reference?

comments.author: PsychronicGames
comments.body: I could see how this could be very useful!

replies.author: PsychronicGames
replies.body:
I'm working on my own game engine too using Three.js for the 3d, so being able to turn the actual models into code is useful in that I might be able to create a 3d model generator, that's not AI in and of itself but lets the users build their own characters like Lego or something:  
[https://psychronic.itch.io/rpg-reactor](https://psychronic.itch.io/rpg-reactor)

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
That actually sounds like a really good fit for img2threejs.

The interesting part is exactly what you described: once the model becomes structured code, you can treat parts like reusable building blocks instead of a fixed asset, swap heads, bodies, armor, materials, proportions, etc. Kind of a procedural LEGO-style character system.

RPG Reactor looks interesting too. I’d love to see how far you can push that workflow.

replies.author: PsychronicGames
replies.body: Yep, I'm still working on it but I am serious about the project being a professional game engine and the results will speak for themselves eventually.

comments.author: aR_ChieYT
comments.body: Was the GLB already modular before becoming editable code or was it modularised before that?

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
The GLB is generated first, then the pipeline processes and modularizes it before converting the result into editable Three.js code.

So the modularization happens before the final code generation step.

replies.author: aR_ChieYT
replies.body: may i ask what you use to modularize ist?

replies.author: Feisty-Scheme-8356
replies.body:
It’s handled by my own custom pipeline. Tripo generates the initial reconstruction, then img2threejs processes the geometry and breaks it down into editable modules before generating the final Three.js code.

You can also take a look directly at the code — img2threejs is fully open source.
